title: BENDING-PATCH: constant-curvature patch test of the Q4 Mindlin plate element

gates.quantity: max |w_h - w_exact| / |w_exact| over affine+skew patches
gates.reference: constant-curvature closed form (patch test, exact reproduction)

gates.reference: constant-curvature closed form

gates.reference: M = Db kappa

gates.reference: 1/2 kappa^T Db kappa * Area (documented: MITC shear sampling on a skew element is not exactly shear-free)

gates.quantity: max displacement error, distorted patch
gates.reference: constant-curvature closed form

gates.reference: the check must reject the wrong rigidity (discriminating power)

gates.quantity: |e(n_y=16) - e(n_y=8)| / e(n_y=16), free lateral, n_x=32
gates.reference: the free-edge leg must be transverse-converged before it is graded

gates.quantity: e(L/b=20) / e(L/b=5), free lateral, n_y=8, fixed element size
gates.reference: clamped-root end effect is local: it must decay with L/b

gates.quantity: observed order of the distorted patch, w (SRI)
gates.reference: second-order consistency of the element (orders below the round-off floor are reported as null, not fitted)

gates.quantity: min tip-deflection error of the locking element (thin strip, t/L = 0.01)
gates.reference: shear locking must be visible (negative control)

gates.quantity: max energy error of the locking element on the patch
gates.reference: shear locking must be visible (negative control)

gates.quantity: observed slope of log(strain-energy error) vs log(h/t), distorted patch, fully integrated 2x2 shear, n=4, t/L = 1 .. 0.05
gates.reference: the spurious transverse-shear energy of the bilinear interpolant scales as (h/t)^2, so a locking element must show slope 2 (a negative control on the law, not on one marginal number); threshold 1.5 = the observed-order floor

gates.quantity: e(h/t=5) / e(h/t=0.25) of the energy error, distorted patch, fully integrated shear, n=4
gates.reference: the (h/t)^2 law predicts 20^2 = 400 over this ladder; a factor 4 slack (>= 100) is required. The round-2 single-point control read 2.1 % against a 2 % threshold (a 5 % margin) at h/t = 0.25, i.e. in the thick-plate regime where locking is weakest by construction

gates.quantity: max strain-energy error of MITC4 over both mesh families and both meshes at t/L = 0.05 (h/t = 5)
gates.reference: assumed transverse-shear strain: the element must stay shear-free in the thin limit, where the locking element is ~558 % off

gates.quantity: max strain-energy error of SRI on the AFFINE patch at t/L = 0.05, both meshes
gates.reference: on an affine mesh the SRI element passes the patch test at every thickness, so distortion -- not thickness -- is the trigger of the degradation measured on the distorted family

gates.quantity: |observed slope - 2| of the SRI energy error vs h/t, distorted patch, n=4
gates.reference: mechanism identification: the SRI degradation must follow the same (h/t)^2 locking law (an implementation error would not reproduce the exponent). SRI reduces the constant ~21x but does not remove the thin-plate limitation on distorted meshes

gates.quantity: max |K_ff u_f + K_fc u_c| over all patch cases
gates.reference: discrete equilibrium

limitations: A patch test is a consistency (necessary) condition; it proves constant-curvature reproduction, not coarse-mesh accuracy or pointwise moment accuracy.
The distorted-patch residual is an interpolation limitation of the bilinear w field (quadratic exact field), measured and h-convergent, not a defect.
A Dirichlet-driven patch contains no zero-energy mode, so this test cannot detect the rank deficiency of the one-point (sri) element.

The free-edge strip leg of the Poisson cross-check is NOT converged at n_y=2: its converged offset is ~1.2% (L/b=5) and it decays with L/b, i.e. it is a clamped-root end effect, not a discretization error. The leg is therefore graded only after transverse convergence, and the coupling itself is graded on the exact M_y=0 state.

The closed-form Poisson ratio is an algebra identity (insensitive to the element); it is reported as an oracle check, not as element evidence. Round 1 graded it as if it were the cross-check -- that gate could not fail.

Literature criterion cited from the standard statement; the textbooks were not retrievable offline, but every target value is evaluated in code from the closed form, so no table digit enters the evidence chain.

THIN-PLATE SCOPE: every graded patch case of rounds 1-2 runs at t/L = 1 (h/t = 0.25), a thick plate. Round 3 thins the plate at a fixed mesh: the relative strain-energy error of the SRI variant follows the (h/t)^2 locking law on DISTORTED meshes (26 % at h/t = 5, n = 4; slope 1.95), while MITC4 and the affine SRI path stay at round-off. The 2 % claims above are therefore certified for h/t <= 0.25; on a general distorted thin-plate mesh MITC4 is the element to use, not SRI.

The thin-limit quantity is the relative error of the discrete strain energy U_h = 1/2 u^T K u, which contains the spurious transverse-shear energy: it is the locking indicator, not a bound on the displacement error (the same SRI cases keep a field-displacement error of a few percent).
